judge_assessment.explanation: All three cited problems check out exactly, and in each case the missing number is printed in the answer key while being absent from verify.json. Problem 6 says 'Write Q1 and Q3 before you subtract --- with 8 values, each half of the data has 4 values in it', and verify.json id 6 is a single stats entry with measure 'iqr' expecting 9; the key computes Q1 = (11+15)/2 = 13 and Q3 = (20+24)/2 = 22 and neither is verified. Problem 8 says 'Find the mean of Team Bravo's scores. Show the total you divided', and id 8 is a single stats entry with measure 'mean' expecting 17; the key displays '8 + 11 + 15 + 15 + 16 + 20 + 24 + 27 = 136' and the 136 is verified nowhere. Problem 9 says 'The second draw comes from a smaller bag than the first --- say what is left before you multiply', and id 9 is a single probability entry favorable 20 total 132 expecting 5/33; the intermediate second-stage 4/11 has no entry. I recomputed everything independently and it is all correct: medians 15.5 and 15.5; ranges 9 and 19; P(blue) = 3/12 = 1/4; Bravo IQR 22 - 13 = 9; (3/8)(1/6) = 3/48 = 1/16; mean 136/8 = 17; (5/12)(4/11) = 20/132 = 5/33; club total 9+6+15+10 = 40 with Robotics 15/40 = 3/8; 1 - (5/8)^2 = 39/64; Alpha IQR (18+19)/2 - (14+15)/2 = 18.5 - 14.5 = 4; and for 12(c) Alpha has 2 scores above 18 and Bravo has 3, giving (2/8)(3/8) = 6/64 = 3/32. All four declared traps compute as stated (15, 27-13 = 14, 136/7 = 19.4286, 3/8+3/8 = 0.75). Problem 12(b) is genuinely manual and correctly declared, matching the judge's manual_items_reviewed = 1.

strengths_to_preserve: The two data sets are engineered so that center cannot separate them: Alpha and Bravo have the identical median 15.5 while their ranges are 9 and 19 and their IQRs 4 and 9. That is the entire point of the comparing-distributions standard, and the key states it twice before problem 12 asks about it -- at problem 2 ('both teams have exactly the same median. Center alone cannot tell these two distributions apart --- that is what problem 12 is about') and at problem 4.

Problem 12 is the correct treatment of a mixed three-part item, and the only one of its kind in my batch: verify.json id 12 carries a stats entry for part (a) (IQR 4), a {"type": "manual"} entry for part (b) whose desc names every element of a full-credit comparison including the specific numbers to cite, and a probability entry for part (c) (3/32). Verified, manual and verified under one id, with the build exiting 2.

Problem 8's key connects the two center measures rather than just computing them: 'Bravo's mean (17) sits above its median (15.5) because the two high scores, 24 and 27, pull the mean upward. The median does not move.' That is the reason a student should care which measure is reported.

Problem 7's grading note actually computes the wrong answer the additive method gives (3/8 + 1/6 = 13/24) and supplies a general sanity check -- '"both" can never be more likely than either part alone'. Problem 11 then makes the complement method the point of the problem, with the additive error (3/8 + 3/8 = 0.75) declared as a machine-checked trap.

The three chance devices are declared once in a shared box at the top (bag: 5 red, 3 blue, 4 green; spinner: 8 sections, 3 red; cube: 1-6), so problems 5, 7, 9 and 11 all draw on one fixed, stated sample space instead of re-specifying it four times. The dot plots and bar chart agree exactly with the score lists and the read_data dictionary -- I checked all 16 dots and all four bar heights.

root_causes.description: Where a stem explicitly demands displayed intermediate work, the verify entry covers only the terminal statistic. Problem 6's Q1 = 13 and Q3 = 22, problem 8's total 136, and problem 9's second-stage 4/11 are all printed responses the stems require ('Write Q1 and Q3 before you subtract', 'Show the total you divided', 'say what is left before you multiply'). Each appears as a finished number in the answer key and in no verify entry, so the key's arithmetic for them is an untested transcription. All three are trivially machine-checkable -- two more stats entries with measure q1/q3, an eval for the sum, and a probability entry for the reduced bag.
evidence: worksheet problem 6: 'Write Q1 and Q3 before you subtract'; verify.json id 6 = one stats entry, measure 'iqr', expected 9
worksheet problem 8: 'Show the total you divided'; verify.json id 8 = one stats entry, measure 'mean', expected 17
worksheet problem 9: 'say what is left before you multiply'; verify.json id 9 = one probability entry, 20/132
answer_key.pdf problem 6 prints Q1 = 13 and Q3 = 22; problem 8 prints the sum 136 -- neither is in verify.json

root_causes.description: The Quick Answers bank hides the sheet's only manual item. Entry 12 reads '4, 3/32' because render_entry() collects only entries that carry an `expected`, and id 12's manual entry has none. A grader scanning the bank sees two answers for a three-part problem with nothing signalling that part (b) exists and must be read by hand. The contrast with a fully manual id, which at least prints '---', is that a partially manual id is silently indistinguishable from a fully covered one.
evidence: worksheet problem 12 prints parts (a), (b) and (c) with answer lines on (a) and (c)
verify.json id 12: stats (4), manual (no expected), probability (3/32)
scripts/render_quick_answers.py render_entry(): 'vals = [e["expected"] for e in entries if isinstance(e, dict) and "expected" in e]'

root_causes.description: All six figures are hand-authored TikZ with render-figures skipped, so the plotted data and the checked data are independent transcriptions. The Alpha dot plot is written as \foreach \p in {12,14,15,16,18,19,21} plus a stacked node at 15, the Bravo plot as {8,11,15,16,20,24,27} plus a stacked node at 15, and the bar chart as coordinates {(1,9) (2,6) (3,15) (4,10)} -- while verify.json separately declares the same values in its stats `data` arrays and its read_data dictionary. They agree here (I compared every dot and bar) but nothing gates it, and every one of the twelve problems is answered by reading these figures or their printed lists.
evidence: worksheet.tex: '\foreach \p in {12,14,15,16,18,19,21}' plus '\node ... at (15,2.8)' for Alpha; '{8,11,15,16,20,24,27}' plus the same stacked node for Bravo

improvements.title: Q1/Q3, the mean's total, and the reduced-bag probability are demanded, printed and unchecked
improvements.proposed_change: Author one entry per printed response, including intermediates the stem explicitly demands. Here: id 6 gains two stats entries with measure 'q1' (expected 13) and 'q3' (expected 22) over the Bravo data; id 8 gains an eval entry for the total (expr '8+11+15+15+16+20+24+27', expected 136); id 9 gains a probability entry for the second stage (favorable 4, total 11) so 'say what is left' is recorded. Enforce systemically with a lint over stems for phrases that name a required intermediate -- 'write X before you', 'show the total', 'say what is left before', 'first find' -- and fail when the id's entry count does not exceed one.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose problem 1 stem is 'Find the interquartile range. Write Q1 and Q3 before you subtract' with a verify JSON holding a single stats/iqr entry; assert the build fails or exits 2 naming the uncovered intermediates. Today curr-200's problem 6 has exactly this shape and every gate passes.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the sole hard failure. All four numbers are already computed in the answer key, so the change records what the key asserts rather than adding content, and it closes the gap on the three problems where the stem makes the intermediate the graded work.
improvements.risk: Medium. The stats type would need q1/q3 measures if it lacks them, and a phrase lint over prose over-flags hints ('first find the probability that neither spin is red' in problem 11 is a strategy hint, not a required response). Ship as exit-2 visibility so a correct build is never blocked.

improvements.title: Bank entry 12 shows two of three parts and gives no sign the third needs manual reading
improvements.proposed_change: Make render_entry() account for entries that carry no `expected`. When an id mixes verified entries with a manual entry, append an explicit marker -- '4, 3/32, (b) manual' -- so the bank tells a grader that part of this problem was not machine-checked. Pair it with rendering fully manual ids as '(manual)' instead of '---', so verified, partially manual and fully manual are three distinguishable states rather than two.
improvements.regression_test: Render a verify JSON where id 12 holds a stats entry (expected 4), a manual entry with no expected, and a probability entry (expected '3/32'); assert the bank line for id 12 contains a manual marker. Fails today: it renders '4, 3/32' with no trace of the manual entry.
improvements.expected_impact: The one item on this sheet a human must actually read stops being invisible in the column a grader scans. The pattern generalises to every multi-part problem that mixes checked and open work, which is the shape SKILL.md should be pushing authors toward.
improvements.risk: Low. The bank is display text never consumed by check_answer_key.py, so the strict per-problem binding gate is unaffected.

improvements.title: Dot plots and bar chart are hand-typed, unbound to the arrays that grade them
improvements.proposed_change: Route the dot plots and the bar chart through scripts/render_figures.py so the drawn dots come from the stats entries' `data` arrays and the bar heights from the read_data `data` dictionary. Where hand-authored TikZ remains, add a gate extracting \foreach point lists and \addplot coordinates from a problem's segment and requiring them to match that id's declared data, failing on any disagreement.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose worksheet draws '\addplot coordinates {(1,9) (2,6) (3,14) (4,10)}' while verify.json id 10 declares data {"Robotics": 15}; assert the build fails naming the mismatch. Today gate_log prints 'render-figures SKIPPED(no figure problems)' and a disagreement of this kind would ship silently.
improvements.expected_impact: Every problem on this sheet is answered from the printed lists or the figures, so a one-digit slip in either the TikZ or the JSON produces a worksheet that contradicts its own verified answer. Binding the two removes the only place where correctness currently rests on care rather than a check.
improvements.risk: Medium. Extracting coordinates from arbitrary TikZ is brittle -- the stacked-dot idiom used here (a \foreach over distinct values plus separate \node entries for repeats) is not trivially parseable -- so the gate should treat unparseable figures as a warning rather than a failure.

case_summary: Strong interleaved statistics-and-probability work. The two score lists are engineered to share a median of 15.5 while their ranges (9 vs 19) and IQRs (4 vs 9) differ sharply, which is exactly the point of the comparing-distributions standard, and the key flags the coincidence twice before problem 12 asks about it. Problem 12 is the best-structured item in my whole batch: part (a) verified (IQR 4), part (b) declared {"type": "manual"} with a desc naming every number a full-credit comparison must cite, part (c) verified (3/32), all under one id with the build exiting 2. Problem 7's grading note computes what the additive error would give and supplies a general sanity check; problem 11 makes the complement the method and declares the additive error as a machine-checked trap; problem 8's key explains why the mean sits above the median. Everything recomputes correctly, and I verified that all 16 dot-plot dots and all four bar heights agree with the declared data. The rejection is right and narrow: problem 6 says 'Write Q1 and Q3 before you subtract' but only the IQR is checked, problem 8 says 'Show the total you divided' but only the mean is checked, and problem 9 says 'say what is left before you multiply' but only the final 5/33 is checked -- while the key prints 13, 22 and 136 as finished numbers with nothing verifying them. Two findings beyond the judge: the Quick Answers bank renders entry 12 as '4, 3/32', silently omitting any sign that part (b) is the sheet's one manual item; and all six figures are hand-authored TikZ with render-figures skipped, so the plotted data and the graded data are independent transcriptions that happen to agree.
